payload.note: [llm audit] The latent heat is computed as H(liquid alloy) minus H(pure-element solids). The real solid of Field's metal (Bi32.5In51Sn16.5) is a eutectic of intermetallic phases (BiIn2 and an In–Sn γ/β solid solution), not elemental Bi, In and Sn. This reference choice, which the agent's own flag records, folds the formation enthalpies of those intermetallics and the liquid mixing enthalpy into the reported value. That biases the latent heat by an amount comparable to the reported uncertainty or larger. The rest of the setup is reasonable for a heavy-metal system: a MACE-MP model on inorganic metals, a 2 fs timestep, 500 atoms and NPT enthalpies at the eutectic temperature.. Fix: Build the solid reference from the actual eutectic phase assemblage, i.e. BiIn2 plus the In–Sn intermetallic or solid solution in the correct lever-rule fractions. Then compute H_liquid − H_solid at the same T and P with multiple seeds. Better still, obtain the latent heat from two-phase coexistence or from a heating/cooling hysteresis of the actual eutectic solid. [claude-opus-5-5, $0.0215]
